title: RacerGS: Residual-Autoregressive Context for 3D Gaussian Splatting Compression
claim: Prior methods suffer from three modeling limitations that cause high per-item coding cost; ours addresses them and shifts the cost distribution lower.
layout: 2 stacked rows split by dashed line, prior above, ours below, plots at right
description: The figure is split by a horizontal dashed line into two rows. The top row is labeled 'Previous Methods'. It has a dashed rounded box listing three limitations: limited spatial context, inefficient entropy modeling, and no causal modeling across anchor feature groups. A cartoon of colored 3D Gaussian ellipsoids sits at the top left. The bottom row sits on a light blue rounded panel labeled 'RacerGS'. It shows a small pipeline: an anchor cube with Gaussians, a stacked feature bar, hash cubes, an MLP, green context bars, and a GRU block with arrows over feature groups, then a black arrow to the results. Each row has the same two plots at right: a histogram of total bits per anchor with a cumulative curve in red, and a line plot of bits per anchor by anchor rank, split into feature, offsets, scaling and XYZ. The bottom row's histogram sits further left and its totals are lower. A bits formula sits above and below, with the residual form in the bottom row.
caption: RacerGS for efficient 3DGS compression. Previous methods have limited spatial context, inefficient entropy modeling, and lack of causal dependencies across anchor feature groups, leading to high coding costs. RacerGS addresses these limitations through compact context projection, residual coding, and autoregressive GRU refinement. This shifts the bitrate distribution toward fewer bits per anchor and lowers total coding costs while preserving rendering fidelity.
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has emerged as a promising approach for fast, high-quality novel-view rendering. However, its large parameter size remains a bottleneck for storage and transmission. We propose RacerGS, a compact 3DGS compression framework that achieves scene reconstruction at significantly reduced storage sizes with preserved fidelity. To obtain compact and spatially coherent features, we design a hash projection model that projects the anchor hash encodings into compact context features. Additionally, we introduce a FiLM-modulated autoregressive GRU context model that utilizes causal dependencies among anchor feature groups and uses recurrent hidden states to refine entropy-model parameters, improving bitrate efficiency. Furthermore, we adaptively entropy-code quantized anchor-attribute residuals relative to their context-predicted means, leveraging spatial consistency to reduce symbol entropy. Overall, RacerGS achieves more than 150x compression over vanilla 3DGS and 28x over Scaffold-GS, while providing comparable rendering quality. Extensive experiments across five datasets demonstrate that RacerGS outperforms prior 3DGS compression methods in both storage reduction and rate-distortion performance.
